## TL;DR
A handoff record stuck at "running" no longer outlives its check. Records not backed by a live process, or older than a newer review verdict or status change, are cleared or reported as stale, and the task card, drawer and CLI show the real state. Move to done is no longer disabled by a stale record when the task is landable.

## Work and rationale
`handoff-status` reconciles a `running` record against live handoff and check processes, the task's status and the latest review pass, and reports `superseded` or `stale` when nothing backs it. The stale flag reaches every checks renderer and the task watchdog no longer writes to held tasks. Post-handoff checkpoint recovery now ignores a crash-orphaned `gate` marker, keeps a pending `review` marker, refuses a second start while the delta review runs, and is single-flight: the handoff slot is claimed synchronously in `startPostHandoffCheckpointRecovery` (a failed claim refuses the start), held through the whole gate and released in a finally. `runner` is now a required dependency, and the third caller in `server.ts` passes it. Tests cover a failed claim, two starts racing, the review-phase cases, a stale record with a newer review pass and with no live process; type check and 141 related tests pass.

## Approaches tried
Reconciling in each renderer, then one server-side reconcile, then phase-scoped marker cleanup, and finally claiming the slot before any await so check-then-act cannot interleave.

## Challenges and blockers
Four review rounds, each finding a narrower lifecycle edge of the same class (who owns a persisted marker). The shots capture timed out once and the first handoffs failed on a consumed report draft.

## Key learnings
Claim exclusivity before any await, and make the dependency that provides it required so a missing one fails loudly instead of silently disabling the guard.
